findings.interpretation: An interactive session of the domain account jdoe on ws01 mapped drive H: to the Users folder of another host's administrative C$ share. Mapping C$ requires administrative rights on 192.0.2.62 and is a common lateral-movement and data-access step; it is also routine for administrators. The memory image shows the command, not whether the mapping succeeded or what was accessed.
findings.observation: In ws01 memory, windows.pstree shows explorer.exe (PID 6664, session 2) started cmd.exe (PID 6784) at 2023-01-25 14:52:04 UTC with the command line 'C:\Windows\system32\cmd.exe /C net use H: \\192.0.2.62\c$\Users', which started net.exe (PID 9128) with 'net  use H: \\192.0.2.62\c$\Users' at the same second. windows.getsids for PID 6784 lists S-1-5-21-1111111111-2222222222-3333333333-1001 jdoe, BUILTIN\Remote Desktop Users and Interactive, at Medium Mandatory Level.
findings.title: ws01: user jdoe mapped the C$ admin share of 192.0.2.62 (net use H: \\192.0.2.62\c$\Users) at 14:52:04 UTC

findings.interpretation: ws01 (192.0.2.61) was a hub of interactive and administrative remote access at capture time: someone was connected to it over RDP from 192.0.2.30 while its explorer.exe held an RDP session onward to 192.0.2.75, and it held SMB sessions both ways. Together with the C$ mapping (F-steve-001) this fits hands-on-keyboard lateral movement, but RDP, SMB and WinRM are also normal administration; the connections alone don't show intent.
findings.observation: windows.netscan on ws01 memory lists, among 170 entries: an inbound RDP connection 192.0.2.30:55264 -> 192.0.2.61:3389 ESTABLISHED (svchost.exe PID 960, TermService) created 14:38:47 UTC; an outbound RDP connection from explorer.exe (PID 6664) 192.0.2.61:59665 -> 192.0.2.75:3389 ESTABLISHED created 14:47:21 UTC; SMB 192.0.2.61:61814 -> 192.0.2.64:445 ESTABLISHED (System) created 14:54:00 UTC; inbound SMB 192.0.2.68:63026 -> 192.0.2.61:445 ESTABLISHED created 14:43:02 UTC; WinRM 192.0.2.61:54867 -> 192.0.2.51:5985 ESTABLISHED (svchost.exe PID 3300, WinRM) created 15:24:11 UTC.
findings.title: ws01 memory: live RDP, SMB and WinRM sessions to and from five internal hosts at capture time (192.0.2.30, 192.0.2.75, 192.0.2.64, 192.0.2.68, 192.0.2.51)

findings.interpretation: The beacon names evil[.]com and evil2[.]com; 203.0.113.7:8443 is the address they resolved to.
findings.observation: svchost.exe (PID 3300) connected to 203.0.113.7:8443 after resolving evil[.]com and evil2[.]com.
findings.title: ws01: beacon to evil[.]com and evil2[.]com at 203.0.113.7:8443
